The Baroque—Hobbes—still has a substantial public sphere.
The Baroque therefore still possesses legitimacy and not merely legality; rule and not merely power.
Louis XIII does not need to fear Richelieu. Only the destruction of dynastic legitimacy beginning with Louis-Philippe clears the road for naked power.
Napoleon I still attempts to establish legitimacy and is, in that sense, still Baroque.
Napoleon III is merely an actor, living off the fruits of earlier ages to the accompaniment of operetta music.

On James Burnham’s The Managerial Revolution: These are discoveries we made twenty or thirty years ago.
If freedom depends on the existence of opposition, who organizes the opposition when everything is organized and even what remains unorganized becomes nothing more than a protected nature reserve?

Does the opposition organize itself freely? Then the ruling elite no longer has it under control. Or is the ruler himself supposed to organize his own opposition, as under Kemal Pasha? Then the whole thing is rigged.

The decisive fact remains that the pressure toward conscious organization, bureaucracy, and planning becomes total. That is Burnham’s starting point too. That is what is current, realistic, suited to the age, and free of illusions.

Why, then, does he suddenly turn toward this contradictory optimism about opposition? How tiny, how minimal, the room left for opposition becomes under total planning! This is still the old idea of opposition that belongs to the spatial imagination of a maritime empire whose ruling class can divide the wealth of the earth among itself—with a free ocean still available!
Once things become serious and bare survival is at stake, games like that come to an end.

Why should I not apply to Myself all the arguments of the ontological proof of God?

“In the end I must withdraw even the half-adequate language I have been using, language I intended to use only for as long as I was still digging around in the entrails of law and at least allowing the word itself to remain.
But once the concept disappears, the word itself truly loses its meaning.
A right can be granted only by a spirit—by God, humanity, or divinity. I demand no right, and therefore I need recognize none.
With absolute right, right itself disappears. The rule of the very concept of right is abolished. I am simply powerful.
If I am powerful, then I am already authorized by that fact alone.
Right is a fixed idea granted by a ghost.
